title: Granular call grouping and time-decay credit allocator PRD
creator: Ananya Patel
description: Problem: Customers with bursty traffic patterns (short-lived fan-out, batching proxies, or chat UIs that re-request the same prompt) get charged for every individual call even when the work is logically a single user action. This leads to noisy invoices and poor UX for quota consumption. Proposal: introduce a server-side 'call grouping' primitive combined with a time-decay credit allocator that groups related API calls into logical transactions and amortizes quota/billing impact for a configurable window. The feature should be opt-in per-organization and visible in the Console and invoices.
background_and_context: Current billing counts per-request token consumption immediately. Many integrations (frontend chat retry, client-side batching, webhooks that fan-out) generate duplicate or near-duplicate requests within small windows. Market differentiator: provide predictable unit economics for real product patterns while keeping accounting auditable. This PRD covers API, billing ledger semantics, console UI, and acceptance criteria for on/off rollout.
goals: Reduce surprising invoice volatility for bursty customers by grouping temporally-related requests into a single logical consumption event
Allow admins to configure grouping window and decay policy to match workload semantics (e.g., 1s for micro-batching, 30s for chat multi-requests)
Ensure billing traceability: every grouped event must map to an auditable set of underlying requests and tokens
Maintain strict SLOs for latency and not add significant overhead to serving runtime
non_goals: Changing per-token pricing or introducing discounts — this is a quota/aggregation mechanism only
Full re-architect of billing pipeline — we will extend existing metering with grouping markers and a small post-process stage
Automated refunds for prior invoices (out of scope for initial launch)
assumptions: We can add a lightweight grouping header to API requests without breaking existing clients
Customers will opt in at the org-level via Console or API flag
The metering pipeline can be extended to ingest grouping tokens and perform aggregation within a short time-window before final ledger write
requirements: API: Add optional header X-Group-Token and X-Group-Window-ms on requests. When present, server will attempt to group calls with identical group token arriving within the configured window (server-enforced, max 60s).
Server semantics: For grouped calls, bill the max token footprint across calls rather than sum (configurable policy: max | sum | capped-sum). Default policy: capped-sum with cap=120% of max footprint

Time-decay credits: When grouping is enabled, allocate a temporal credit budget that decays linearly over the group window; unused credit is not credited back to past invoices but will reduce immediate counted consumption inside that window
Audit trail: Metering records must include group_token, individual_request_ids, individual_token_counts, aggregated_billed_tokens, grouping_policy, and grouping_window_ms
Console: Show grouped events in per-route dashboards with an option to toggle expanded view (show underlying requests) and a chart of grouping rate and estimated savings
Billing/export: Invoice line items must include an optional grouped label and reference to a downloadable CSV that contains the underlying request-level rows
Fallback: If a request lacks X-Group-Token, behavior unchanged. If grouping metadata is malformed, reject header and proceed ungrouped, emitting a metric
Edge cases: Streaming responses must still record token counts per chunk; grouping uses final total per-request. Retries should carry same group token to be deduplicated where possible
detailed_examples: Example A (chat re-request): Client sends two identical messages within 500ms with same X-Group-Token. Token footprints: 120 and 125. With default capped-sum cap=120% of max: max=125, cap=150 (120%*125) -> aggregated billed tokens = min(sum=245, cap=150) = 150. Customer sees single grouped line item for 150 tokens instead of two line items (245).

Example B (frontend retry): Client retries a request due to network glitch. Same group token arrives twice; second request marked as retry in audit and not double-billed if within window and identical request id metadata present

Example C (embed vs generate mix): Grouping only applies for homogeneous operation types by default (e.g., group embedding calls separately from generation). Admins can enable cross-type grouping at org-level but must accept reduced fidelity in per-operation metrics
api_spec_notes: Header X-Group-Token: opaque UUID chosen by client or server-assigned (string up to 128 chars)
Header X-Group-Window-ms: desired client hint; server will clamp to organization max (admin setting) and global max 60000ms
Response: Server returns X-Group-Applied: true|false and X-Grouping-Event-Id when grouping was used
Metering payload: include field grouping_event_id and flattened request list for downstream billing consumers
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for grouping selection logic (identical token, time window boundaries, malformed headers)

Integration test in staging: when grouping enabled, e2e invoice preview aggregates grouped requests per policy and matches expected numbers for three workloads (chat retries, batched clients, streaming chunks)
Console UI shows grouped events with correct expanded audit CSV download that contains original request IDs and token counts
Billing export CSV includes grouping_event_id column and aggregated_billed_tokens matches ledger writes
No measurable increase (>5ms p95) in API request latency in canary traffic with grouping header present
Metrics: internal metric grouping_applied_rate, grouping_conflict_rate, grouping_malformed_header_rate are emitted and surfaced in ops dashboard
Fallback safety: If metering pipeline ingestion fails to apply grouping, individual requests are billed normally and an alert triggers a one-off reconciliation job
metrics_and_success_criteria: Invoice volatility reduction: target 25% reduction in week-over-week variance for pilot customers over first 30 days
Adoption: 10 pilot customers enabled within first 6 weeks
Accuracy: 100% of grouped events in pilot must have full audit rows available for download
Performance: p99 tail latency delta < 10ms for grouping-enabled requests
security_and_compliance: Grouping tokens must not encode PII; enforce max length and character whitelist
Audit CSVs are stored behind org ACL and follow existing retention policies
If grouping metadata surfaces customer-specific logic, ensure RBAC prevents cross-org grouping
dependencies: ENG-75412 (metering pipeline extension for grouping markers)
ENG-76104 (Console UI: grouped events view + CSV export)
ENG-74590 (runtime header passthrough and lightweight grouping cache)
BI-3401 (billing ledger mapping for grouped events)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dogfood behind feature flag with opt-in orgs; monitor metrics for 7 days
Phase 1: limited pilot (10 customers) enabled via SEs; collect invoice feedback and audit CSVs
Phase 2: GA opt-in toggle in Console and org-level API flag; documentation and SDK examples
Phase 3: optional default-on for some plan tiers after 90 days if adoption and savings validated
rollout_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: grouping may hide abuse patterns — Mitigation: preserve full request-level audit and add anomaly detection on grouped patterns
Risk: downstream billing consumers misinterpret aggregated rows — Mitigation: include clear schema versioning in exports and backward-compatible fields
Risk: incorrect grouping windows cause undercount — Mitigation: conservative default policy (capped-sum) and admin visibility to tune
open_questions: Should grouping be allowed across org members or restricted to a single API key? Proposed: restrict by API key by default, allow cross-key grouping if org-admin enables
What is the default grouping window per product (chat vs embeddings)? Proposed defaults: chat=30s, generate=5s, embed=1s
How to handle mixed-operation groupings for hybrid SDKs? Require explicit cross-type opt-in in org settings
implementation_notes: Work to be done across runtime (fast in-memory grouping cache keyed by group_token + org_id), metering staging buffer to apply aggregation before ledger write, Console UI changes for org settings and grouped event drill-down, and billing export schema updates. Use feature flags and a migration mode that includes both grouped and ungrouped counts for the first 14 days for auditing.
